## Answered: one flaky test, diagnosed and carded. Closing.

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`.

### What was red

Exactly two jobs of 17 in run [34313211319](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34313211319) — `Test Core (4/6)` and the `Test Core` aggregate it fails. Everything else concluded `success` (tally: 15 success, 2 failure). One package, one test, one assertion:

```
FAIL src/turso-driver-timeout.test.ts > TursoDriverConfig.timeout — remote mode over HTTP
     > a stalled remote fails the operation within the configured window, as TIMEOUT / 504
AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0   ❯ :122:31
Test Files  1 failed | 49 passed (50)
Tests       1 failed | 1230 passed (1231)
```

The operation *did* fail as `TIMEOUT` / 504 inside its window — every assertion about the driver passed. What failed is the epilogue `expect(remote.requests()).toBeGreaterThan(0)`: the test gives the client **100 ms** (`WINDOW_MS`) to get bytes onto a local socket while six shards run concurrently on the runner.

### It is non-deterministic, and that is measured rather than assumed

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| next hourly run, [34317273493](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34317273493) at 06:01Z | **success** |
| ⭐ `git diff --stat 041d9fdc68 a016f08b8a -- packages/drivers/driver-turso/` | **empty — untouched** |
| control: what did change between those commits | 24 files, 2,966 insertions |

⇒ Identical driver code, identical test, red then green. ⛔ Nothing to bisect and no infrastructure fault to blame.

⚠️ I nearly closed this on "the next run was green", which would have been wrong: the green run is on a **different commit**, so on its own it proves only that `a016f08b8a` is green. The untouched-package diff is what makes it a flake.

### Filed

**#17079** — the race, both call sites (`:122` and `:138` carry the same assertion; only the first has been observed losing), and three candidate directions left explicitly unprejudged. ⛔ Ungraded and unlabelled: `domain:*` is triage's.

### Closing, and a note on this card's own machinery

Closing per this card's rule — *"a card nobody reopens is closed by the next green run being uneventful"* — with the diagnosis carded so nothing is lost.

⚠️ Worth stating for the next reader, because I checked and briefly misread it: `scheduled-full-run-card.yml` **has no close path and is not supposed to have one**. Its job guard is `conclusion == 'failure' || conclusion == 'timed_out'`, so it only ever files or refreshes; closing is a seat's act, which is consistent with its own ⛔ *"A CLOSED card is never reopened. Red again after it was answered is a regression, filed fresh."* The six most recent runs of that workflow all conclude `skipped` — that is the guard working on non-schedule events, ⛔ not a broken watcher.

⇒ The #16467 machinery did exactly what it was built for: a red on `main` that blocks nothing and notifies nobody got a card, a diagnosis and a follow-up card within two hours.
